repairs.before: Your Highness holds the duty of the bulwark city—you ought deeply to ponder it.
repairs.after: Your Highness holds the responsibility of a bulwark of the ruling house. You should consider this deeply.
repairs.reason: 維城 describes a royal kinsman's role as the dynasty's bulwark.
repairs.reviewReason: 維城之任 denotes the responsibility of a royal kinsman as a bulwark of the ruling house, not an office in a literal bulwark city. The replacement preserves the address and injunction to consider the matter deeply; s0040 repeats 維城 in the same dynastic-protection context. The paired idiomatic field already conveys that responsibility.

repairs.before: At the time Director Wang Min and right aide Guo Bo, because punishments and government were too lenient, debated wishing for harsh regulation. Hong said, "When human feelings are humiliated, a fierce and stern mind arises;
repairs.after: At the time, Master of Writing Wang Min and Right Assistant Director Guo Bo considered the administration of punishments too lenient and discussed imposing stricter rules. Hong said, “When people are thwarted and humiliated, a fierce spirit rises in them.
repairs.reason: The two offices should be rendered accurately in the parallel literal field; 右丞 specifies the right assistant director.
repairs.reviewReason: 尚書王敏 and 右丞郭播 identify Wang Min as Master of Writing and Guo Bo as Right Assistant Director. The replacement preserves both officials, their judgment that penal administration is too lenient, the proposal for stricter rules, and Hong’s ensuing observation that humiliation produces a fierce spirit. It agrees with the paired field and the chapter’s 尚書 usage in s0008; the quotation continues in s0010.

repairs.before: Hong sent Rear General Yao Ping to rescue him; Sheng withdrew.
repairs.after: Hong sent Rear General Yao Ping to its relief, and Sheng withdrew.
repairs.reason: The threatened place is Qinzhou, not a named male rescuee. Tongjian 117 also has Qin's rear general come to its aid.
repairs.reviewReason: In s0055 Yang Sheng captures Qishan and presses Qinzhou; 救之 in s0056 therefore sends Yao Ping to the threatened place’s relief. The replacement removes the misleading male rescuee while preserving Hong’s dispatch, Yao Ping’s Rear General title, and Sheng’s withdrawal. The paired field explicitly names Qinzhou, consistent with the later Qinzhou sequence.

repairs.before: Yao Shao and General Who Captures Barbarians Yin Zhao, General Who Guards the Army Yao Qia, and others led fifty thousand foot and horse to campaign against Bobo; Yao Hui with ten thousand picked cavalry followed them.
repairs.after: Yao Shao, General Who Campaigns against the Enemy Yin Zhao, General Who Guards the Army Yao Qia and others led fifty thousand infantry and cavalry against Bobo. Yao Hui followed with ten thousand picked cavalry.
repairs.reason: 征虜 is an expeditionary generalship and does not denote taking captives.
repairs.reviewReason: 征虜 is the campaign-against-the-enemy generalship borne by Yin Zhao, not a title meaning capture of barbarians. The replacement preserves Yao Shao, Yin Zhao, Yao Qia, the fifty-thousand infantry-and-cavalry force against Bobo, and Yao Hui’s following ten-thousand picked cavalry. The paired field has the same corrected title and force accounting; later references retain these officers without conflicting title translations.

repairs.before: Yao Shao advanced and said, "Your Majesty not forgetting to repay virtue—enfeoffing them is right; the ancients respected the affair and charged them with its beginning—it is possible to wait until next spring, then deliberate."
repairs.after: Yao Shao stepped forward and said, “Your Majesty remembers to repay virtue; enfeoffing them is right. The ancients treated such matters with reverence and made appointments at the beginning of the year. You could wait until next spring and then consider it.”
repairs.reason: The proposed timing in the next clause explains 以始; 'charged them with its beginning' obscures the timing of appointments.
repairs.reviewReason: 古者敬其事，命之以始 links reverent handling of the appointments to their appropriate beginning; 可須來春 supplies the next-spring timing. The replacement makes that timing intelligible instead of “charged them with its beginning,” and retains Shao’s support for enfeoffment as repayment of virtue and his advice to defer deliberation. The paired field conveys the same proposition; s0052 records that Hong desists.

repairs.before: Hong sent Colonel of Agile Cavalry Yan Sheng with three thousand horse to hurry there, Martial Guard Yao Yinan leading ten thousand foot soldiers to assist in guarding Luoyang, and also sent General Who Conquers the East and shepherd of Bingzhou Yao Yi to camp south at Shan ford as sounding support.
repairs.after: Hong sent Yan Sheng, colonel of the Yue Cavalry, with three thousand horsemen to the rescue. Martial Guard commander Yao Yinan led ten thousand infantry to help defend Luoyang. Hong also sent Yao Yi, General Who Conquers the East and governor of Bingzhou, south to camp at Shan Ford in support.
repairs.reason: The parallel literal rendition adds 'agile' and misses that 牧 is a governorship.
repairs.reviewReason: 越騎校尉 is the colonel of the Yue Cavalry and 并州牧 is the governorship of Bingzhou. The replacement accurately retains the three separate commands: Yan Sheng with three thousand horsemen to the rescue, Yao Yinan with ten thousand infantry to assist Luoyang, and Yao Yi moving south to Shan Ford in support. The paired field agrees; s0117 preserves the separate Yan Sheng/Yao Yinan movements, and s0119 and s0131 corroborate Shan Ford.

repairs.before: What will you tell the emperor when he asks where the granaries went?"
repairs.after: If the court questions Your Highness, what will you say in reply?”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 若朝廷問殿下者，將何辭以報

repairs.reason: The officials ask what Yi can say in reply if the court questions him. The text never says the granary buildings themselves disappeared.
repairs.reviewReason: 若朝廷問殿下者，將何辭以報 asks conditionally what His Highness could answer if questioned by the court. The replacement preserves that conditional challenge without inventing an imperial question about missing granary buildings. The preceding grain-distribution context and the paired literal field support it.

repairs.before: Shi Wuhui broke at Stone Pass and ran.
repairs.after: Shi Wuhui reached Stone Pass and fled back.
repairs.reason: Wuhui reaches the pass and flees back; no fighting or breaking of his formation is stated.
repairs.reviewReason: 至石關，奔還 states that Wuhui reached Stone Pass and fled back; it does not state that his formation broke in combat. The replacement preserves the destination and return direction. Shi Wuhui is explicitly identified in s0107, and the paired literal field already has this reading.

repairs.before: Mao Dezu attacked Hongnong Grand Administrator Yin Ya at Li city; the host broke; Dezu sent cavalry pursuing and seized him; afterward he killed the Jin guards and fled to firm Tong Pass.
repairs.after: Mao Dezu attacked Yin Ya, governor of Hongnong, at Li city. Ya’s troops broke, and Dezu sent cavalry in pursuit and captured him. Later Ya killed his Jin guards and fled to hold Tong Pass.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 既而殺晉守者奔固潼關

repairs.reason: Yin Ya is the captive who later kills his Jin guards and flees to defend the pass; 'firm Tong Pass' obscures the action.
repairs.reviewReason: The subject captured by Dezu’s pursuing cavalry is Yin Ya. In the following clause it is that captive who kills his Jin guards and flees to hold Tong Pass. The replacement makes the subject change and 奔固 action clear while preserving the attack at Li city and Ya’s Hongnong office. The paired field and the Yin Ya references in s0161 and s0191 are consistent with this reading.

repairs.before: No Hedong troops joined Yao Yi; he panicked.
repairs.after: No troops from Hedong went over to Yao Yi, and this worried him deeply.
repairs.reason: Yi is deeply troubled at the refusal of the Hedong troops; panic is a stronger emotion than 患 here.
repairs.reviewReason: 河東之兵無詣懿者 says that no Hedong troops came over to Yi; 懿深患之 says that this deeply troubled him. The replacement preserves the refusal and its emotional effect without overstating 患 as panic. The paired literal field and the surrounding rebellion narrative agree.

repairs.before: Hu Yidu objected: "Split the army and one defeat routs every heart—you cannot fight divided."
repairs.after: Hu Yidu, one of Shao’s generals, said, “We must concentrate our forces and keep them together. If a detachment suffers a reverse, the men will be seized with fear. How could we fight then?”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 若偏師不利，人心駭懼，胡可以戰

repairs.reason: Hu distinguishes the risk to a single detachment from its effect on the whole army's morale.
repairs.reviewReason: 軍勢宜集不可以分 requires keeping the forces concentrated; 若偏師不利 identifies a reverse suffered by a detachment, followed by fear among the men and the rhetorical question about fighting. The replacement retains each proposition. The preceding speech in s0197–s0199 establishes Yao Shao as the commander, so “one of Shao’s generals” correctly resolves 其將; the paired literal field and other Hu Yidu occurrences are consistent.

repairs.before: the wicked heir lost his plan, tied cord and surrendered at Zhidao.
repairs.after: The wicked heir lost his plan and surrendered with a cord about his neck, as the Qin ruler had at Zhidao.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 凶嗣失圖，系組而降軹道

repairs.reason: The appraisal echoes Qin ruler Ziying's surrender in Shiji 6, including the neck cord and Zhidao. Distinguish its allusion from the narrative surrender at the camp gate in s0245.
repairs.reviewReason: The appraisal’s 系組而降軹道 invokes the Qin surrender motif, rather than establishing Zhidao as the literal site of Hong’s narrative surrender. The local primary witness, Shiji 006 s0664, explicitly gives Ziying’s neck cord and surrender beside Zhidao. The replacement marks the allusion and preserves the wicked heir’s failed plan; the paired field already marks the comparison. It leaves s0245’s surrender with wife and children at the camp gate intact and grants no independent chronology or identity approval.

repairs.before: Thus the wheel turns: extremes invite reversal.
repairs.after: When things reach their extreme, they reverse course. Is this what the saying means?
repairs.reason: The historian closes with a rhetorical question about reversal at extremes; there is no wheel in the source.
repairs.reviewReason: 物極則反 states reversal at an extreme, and 抑斯之謂歟 is the historian’s rhetorical question about whether this is what the saying means. The replacement conveys both propositions without the unsupported wheel image. The paired literal field also retains reversal and an interrogative ending.

repairs.before: They sent Hong to Jiankang market and beheaded him; he was thirty years old, on the throne two years.
repairs.after: They sent Hong to Jiankang and beheaded him in the marketplace. He was thirty years old and had been on the throne for two years.
repairs.reason: The destination is Jiankang; the marketplace is specifically the site of the beheading.
repairs.reviewReason: 送泓于建康市斬之 sends Hong to Jiankang and specifies the marketplace as the execution setting. The replacement preserves both, together with 時年三十 and 在位二年, without treating “Jiankang market” as the destination’s name. The paired field has the same reading. This accepts the English rendering of the stated age and reign duration, not a chronology certification.

repairs.before: Hong proposed making sixteen palace officers viscounts or barons. Yao Zan objected, “Surely the crown prince’s civil and military officers owe him loyalty as a matter of duty. They have shown no conspicuous merit. Why grant them so many fiefs?”
repairs.after: Hong proposed making sixteen palace officers viscounts or barons under the five-rank system of nobility. Yao Zan objected, “Surely the crown prince’s civil and military officers owe him loyalty as a matter of duty. They have shown no conspicuous merit. Why grant them so many fiefs?”
repairs.reason: 五等 explicitly names the five-grade nobility framework as well as the two ranks 子男; the accepted literal already includes this. This is the only 五等 occurrence in this chapter.
repairs.reviewReason: 五等 explicitly supplies the five-rank nobility framework, while 子男 supplies the viscount/baron ranks. The replacement retains both, all sixteen palace officers, Yao Zan’s remonstrance, their Eastern Palace duty of loyalty, the absence of conspicuous merit, and his question about so many fiefs. The paired literal field already includes the framework; 五等 has no other chapter occurrence.

repairs.before: Before long Jin Grand Commandant Liu Yu commanded the great host to campaign against Hong, halted at Pengcheng, sent General Who Wins the Championship Tan Daoji and General Who Soars like Dragon Wang Zhen'e in from Huai and Fei to attack Qiqiu and Xiangcheng, General Shen Linzi from Bian into the He to attack Cangyuan.
repairs.after: Before long Liu Yu, grand commandant of Jin, led a great army against Hong and halted at Pengcheng. He sent Champion General Tan Daoji and Dragon-Soaring General Wang Zhen'e in by the Huai and Fei rivers to attack Qiqiu and Xiangcheng. General Shen Linzi went from the Bian into the Yellow River to attack Cangyuan.
repairs.reason: 冠軍將軍 is the military rank Champion General. Both fields of the only other occurrence of 冠軍 (s0131), and s0080 idiomatic, already use Champion General. The replacement preserves 劉裕’s command, officers and titles, Shen’s separate route and objectives.
repairs.reviewReason: 冠軍將軍 is the rank Champion General, as already rendered in both fields at s0131. The replacement preserves Liu Yu’s command and halt at Pengcheng, Tan Daoji and Wang Zhen’e with their titles and Huai/Fei approach to Qiqiu and Xiangcheng, and Shen Linzi’s separate Bian-to-Yellow-River approach to Cangyuan. The paired field and s0081’s Qiqiu/Xiangcheng sequence agree; no officer, route, or objective is dropped.
